_README: PRODUCER ANCHORS -- data-driven input to ci-hub/validate/preflight_anchor.py.
THE PRODUCER TRAVELS WITH THE BRANCH. A hermit/reverie checkout runs ITS OWN
validate.sh; that producer emits exactly the receipt fields the producer's
commit knew how to emit. Any consumer-side receipt requirement added AFTER a
PR was branched (e.g. is_clean_full_pass in ci-hub/lib/validate_status.rs)
is UNSATISFIABLE by that PR until it rebases onto the commit that taught the
producer to emit the field. A head that predates such a commit will run a
full, green, exit-0 validate whose ledger record is nonetheless rejected
(the required field is NULL) -- a doomed ~17-minute run.
Each object below is ONE such tightening: `sha` is the commit that makes the
producer emit `field`; a head that does NOT contain `sha` cannot self-certify
and preflight_anchor.py REFUSES it before validate starts (2s, not 17min).
ADD A NEW ENTRY HERE whenever a receipt-schema requirement is tightened. Its
`sha` is the commit on rrnewton/hermit:main that makes the producer
(validate.sh / its aggregate helpers) emit the newly-required field. Until
that commit lands, leave the entry out (or commented in `_pending`) -- an
anchor with a placeholder SHA would refuse every head.
